full_revised_card.card: Despite its familiar name, the Bayeux Tapestry is embroidery rather than a woven pictorial tapestry. Wool stitches form the narrative on joined linen panels. Examining the stitched surface offers a concrete way to distinguish applied needlework from an image created by weaving.

evidence.note: Wool embroidery, joined linen and narrative construction are explicit.

relations.note: Construction and narrative imagery make the object evidence about both making and historical representation.

full_revised_card.label: Under the Wave off Kanagawa
full_revised_card.learning_takeaway: Hokusai uses perspective and framing to make Mount Fuji appear as a small triangular form within the much larger wave.
full_revised_card.card: Hokusai’s Under the Wave off Kanagawa makes Mount Fuji appear as a small triangular form within a towering wave. The contrast depends on perspective and framing. Looking between the mountain and the water reveals how the print organizes apparently unequal scales within one view.

evidence.note: Fuji’s small triangular appearance within the wave is explicitly attributed to perspective.

relations.note: The museum’s named woodblock print provides a specific case of image construction through printmaking.
